title: Beyond breathing: multimodal pathways connecting olfaction to autonomic nervous system modulation
title_zh: 超越呼吸：连接嗅觉与自主神经系统调节的多模态通路
abstract: The interaction between olfaction and respiration has recently emerged as a central aspect of brain-body interactions. To date, most studies in this context, both in rodents and humans, have focused on how respiratory airflow rhythmically drives brain activity. In this review, we shift the focus to the modulatory effects of odorant molecules, which engage chemical, affective, and trigeminal pathways to elicit integrated sensory experiences and robust autonomic responses. We synthesize recent findings showing that the olfactory system, through its unique connectivity with limbic and autonomic networks, operates at the interface between exteroception and interoception. By modulating respiratory dynamics, and more generally autonomic nervous system activity, odors emerge as a multimodal signal capable of influencing brain-body interactions and supporting well-being.
abstract_zh: 嗅觉与呼吸的相互作用最近被认为是脑-体相互作用的核心方面。迄今为止，在此背景下的研究大多集中于呼吸气流节律如何驱动脑活动。本综述将焦点转向气味分子对调节的影响，它们通过化学、情感和三叉神经通路激发综合感官体验和强烈的自主反应。我们综合了最新发现，表明嗅觉系统通过其与边缘和自主网络的独特连通性，位于外感知与内感知之间的接口。通过调节呼吸动力学以及更广泛的自主神经系统活动，气味成为一种多模态信号，能够影响脑-体相互作用并支持健康福祉。
